title: Platform benefit-cost ratio
caption: A platform repays when recovered engineering time, valued at loaded hourly cost, exceeds the platform's total cost. The ratio is linear in model count: the 50-model scenario in the chapter reaches 1.25 and the 20-model scenario 0.5.

symbols.name: benefit-cost ratio
symbols.meaning: gross recovered-capacity value divided by total platform cost; 1 is break-even, above 1 is net return

symbols.name: model count
symbols.meaning: production models whose toil the platform absorbs

symbols.name: hours saved per model-month
symbols.meaning: engineering hours the platform recovers per model per month; the chapter's LEGO scenario uses 40

symbols.name: loaded engineer cost
symbols.meaning: fully loaded hourly cost of an ML engineer, about 150 dollars per hour in the chapter scenarios

symbols.name: platform total cost
symbols.meaning: annual running cost of the platform team plus its infrastructure

title: Feature freshness latency
caption: Freshness is measured on availability time, the moment the feature store can serve the value, not the event time the underlying fact happened. Backfills and late arrivals make the two clocks diverge, so watermarks bound the gap.

symbols.name: freshness latency
symbols.meaning: how stale a served feature value is, in time units

symbols.name: availability time
symbols.meaning: when the feature record became queryable in the store

symbols.name: event time
symbols.meaning: when the source event that produced the feature occurred

title: A/B sample size per variant
caption: Two-proportion sizing for one variant: baseline rate p, detectable absolute difference delta, z_alpha for confidence and z_beta for power. Detecting a 10 percent relative lift on a 5 percent click-through rate needs about 30,000 samples per variant; a 1 percent baseline at 5 percent relative needs about 621,000.

symbols.name: samples per variant
symbols.meaning: independent observations needed in each arm of the experiment

symbols.name: confidence quantile
symbols.meaning: z-score for the chosen confidence level; 1.96 at 95 percent

symbols.name: power quantile
symbols.meaning: z-score for statistical power; 0.84 at 80 percent power

symbols.name: baseline rate
symbols.meaning: expected outcome proportion under control, e.g. click-through rate

symbols.name: detectable difference
symbols.meaning: smallest absolute change worth detecting, e.g. 0.005 for half a percentage point

title: Rollout exposure risk
caption: Release risk prices the probability of regression times the impact per exposed unit times the number of units exposed. A 5 percent canary cuts blast radius twentyfold against a 100 percent cutover, and stage duration is set by required samples over traffic rate times traffic fraction.

symbols.name: rollout risk
symbols.meaning: expected harm from a release, in impact-weighted exposed units

symbols.name: regression probability
symbols.meaning: estimated chance the candidate degrades the guarded metric

symbols.name: impact per unit
symbols.meaning: harm each exposed unit suffers if the regression ships

symbols.name: exposed units
symbols.meaning: requests, users or regions receiving the candidate during a stage

title: SLO vector consumption
caption: Each reliability dimension consumes a fraction of its error budget. The fleet is healthy only when the worst dimension stays at or below one; the chapter's example has freshness at 1.30 while the mean of 0.70 hides it.

symbols.name: observed violations
symbols.meaning: budget-consuming events observed on dimension d in the window

symbols.name: allowed budget
symbols.meaning: violations permitted on dimension d before the SLO breaks

symbols.name: worst dimension
symbols.meaning: the single reliability dimension closest to or past its limit

title: Fleet false-alert probability
caption: Independent monitors multiply false crossings. One hundred models with ten metrics each, checked every five minutes at a 0.003 false-positive rate, produce about 864 raw false crossings per day; loosening to two sigma pushes the daily count past 14,000.

symbols.name: false-positive rate
symbols.meaning: probability one monitor check crosses its threshold with nothing wrong

symbols.name: monitor checks
symbols.meaning: models times metrics times checks per day; the chapter's example is 288,000

symbols.name: at least one false crossing
symbols.meaning: probability the fleet sees a false alarm somewhere, which approaches one as N grows

title: Canary stage duration
caption: Stage length is set by the experiment's sample requirement divided by request rate times traffic fraction. At 1 million requests per hour and 10,000 required samples, a 1 percent stage needs about an hour and a 5 percent stage about 12 minutes; delayed labels and guardrail windows can extend it.

symbols.name: stage duration
symbols.meaning: time a rollout stage must run to collect its required evidence

symbols.name: required samples
symbols.meaning: observations per variant the evaluation contract demands, e.g. 10,000 guardrail samples

symbols.name: traffic rate
symbols.meaning: requests per unit time arriving at the service

symbols.name: traffic fraction
symbols.meaning: share of traffic routed to the candidate during the stage, e.g. 0.01 for canary

title: ML total cost of ownership
caption: The four cost planes over one horizon with no double counting. The chapter's constructed budgets show iteration dominating a startup at 84 percent of monthly cost while inference dominates a 50-model production fleet at 41 percent; the dominant term changes over the lifecycle.

symbols.name: training cost
symbols.meaning: GPU time, energy and failure overhead for model training runs

symbols.name: inference cost
symbols.meaning: provisioned accelerator capacity serving live traffic at its SLO

symbols.name: data cost
symbols.meaning: storage, egress and processing for feature and training data

symbols.name: iteration cost
symbols.meaning: engineering time and compute per experiment, including the roughly nine in ten that improve nothing
